label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 1 · Question 19

hints.title: Separate the signs of the input
hints.body: Rewrite the absolute value using separate rules for negative and nonnegative x.
hints.recap: The modulus of x equals x on the nonnegative side and minus x on the negative side.
hints.pitfall: The derivative in the question must be nonnegative on both half-axes.
hints.pause: Write the two polynomial derivative expressions.

recall.reminder: The modulus of x equals x on the nonnegative side and minus x on the negative side.

hints.title: Integrate both pieces and inspect the join
hints.body: Apply the power rule on each side, then compare the resulting pieces with the options. Check that the chosen expression is also defined and differentiable at zero.
hints.recap: An absolute-value formula changes at its breakpoint, so integrate the pieces separately.
hints.pitfall: Matching the derivative only for positive x is not enough.
hints.pause: Find one expression valid for all real x and verify its behaviour at zero.

recall.reminder: An absolute-value formula changes at its breakpoint, so integrate the pieces separately.

solution:
1. Resolve the modulus. |−6x|=6|x|, which is 6x for x≥0 and −6x for x<0.

2. Integrate on each side. The corresponding primitives are 3x2+C on the nonnegative side and −3x2+C on the negative side. The constants must agree at zero because a differentiable solution is continuous.

3. Write and check one expression. These pieces combine as 3x|x|+C. At zero, the derivative of 3x|x| is the limit of 3h|h|/h=3|h|, which is zero, agreeing with the required derivative. Thus f(x)=3x|x|. Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Integrate an absolute-value derivative on both half-axes and check the join
